body.statement: \(\textsc{Explicit-Max-Tail}\), whose encoded instance consists of \(a\), a rational \(\delta\), every labeled rational coordinate \(y_i^{\mathrm{obs},\delta}\) with \(i\notin M(a)\), the support \(\Omega\) listed row by row, every rational weight \(w_z\), and a rational threshold \(q\), is NP-complete. Membership in NP is certified by a complete weak order together with a rational representative \(b\in\mathcal C_\delta(a)\) of polynomial encoding length; a polynomial-time verifier checks the observed-coordinate equalities, the represented weak order and midranks, and the exact rational weighted tail inequality \(p(a,b)\ge q\). NP-hardness holds for instances \(\mathsf R(G,s)\) with \(v\) missing realized-treated outcomes, four realized controls, two distinct observed outcome values, \(n=3v-s+4\) units, and \(1+2v+|E|\) explicitly listed rows with polynomial-bit rational weights. For every reduced instance with \(|E|\ge\binom{s}{2}\), the graph \(G\) has an \(s\)-clique if and only if some completion reaches \(q_\star\); moreover, every completion reaching \(q_\star\) has exactly \(s\) passing vertex rows whose labels form the unique lowest tied block and induce an \(s\)-clique in \(G\).
body.justification: The result shows that the chamber explosion reflects intrinsic completion difficulty rather than a naive implementation.
body.gap: The exact-test literature reports combinatorial cost but supplies no decision-complexity classification for a rationally weighted explicit support with missing midranks.
body.consumer: Software can justify exact fixed-\(k\) computation and principled approximation when attrition is large.
body.proof_tex:
We first prove membership in \(\mathrm{NP}\).  A certificate gives a complete weak order of the \(n\) labels and the polynomial-length rational representative guaranteed by the weak-order-attainment theorem.  The verifier checks every fixed observed coordinate, checks all pairwise relations asserted by the ordered partition, and computes each doubled block midrank \(2c+d+1\).  It then computes the \(L\) doubled treated-rank sums, compares each with the realized sum, and accumulates the listed rational weights exactly.  All integers and common-denominator rational sums have polynomial encoding length in \(\ell\).  The verifier accepts exactly when the resulting value is at least \(q\).  Conversely, if a real completion is accepted, its compatible weak-order cell has the same tail and has such a rational representative.  Hence \(\textsc{Explicit-Max-Tail}\in\mathrm{NP}\).

For hardness, use the cited NP-completeness of \(\textsc{Clique}\).  Let \((G,s)\) have \(V=\{1,\ldots,v\}\), \(2\le s\le v\), and \(e=|E|\).  If \(e<\binom{s}{2}\), the source instance is certainly negative; map it to a fixed negative instance, for example two fully observed units of values \(1,0\), the two one-treated assignments of weight \(1/2\), the higher-valued unit realized treated, and threshold \(1\).  Its only oracle tail is \(1/2\), so this is a valid negative output.  It remains to treat \(e\ge\binom{s}{2}\).

Set
\[
h=2v-s,\qquad B=e+1,\qquad A_\star=vB+e+1,
\]
and construct \(\mathsf R(G,s)\) as in the guard--vertex--edge definition, with \(\delta=0\).  There are \(v\) missing vertex labels, \(h\) observed anchors of value \(1\), and four observed controls of value \(0\).  The realized row treats all vertex and anchor labels.  Its treated count is \(m=v+h\).  Every guard, vertex, and edge row makes an equal-sized exchange, so every row also belongs to \(\mathcal Z_m\).  Since \(h=2v-s\ge2\), all named anchor exchanges exist.  Rows from different categories treat respectively one, two, or four controls, while rows within a category remove distinct labeled vertices or vertex pairs; hence all listed rows are distinct.  Their count and the total number of units are
\[
L=1+2v+e,
\qquad
n=v+h+4=3v-s+4.
\]
Give the actual, guard, vertex, and edge rows unnormalized weights \(1,A_\star,B,1\), respectively.  The normalizer and threshold are
\[
W_\star=1+vA_\star+vB+e,
\qquad
q_\star=\frac{1+vA_\star+sB+\binom{s}{2}}{W_\star}.
\]
Because \(s\le v\) and \(\binom{s}{2}\le e\), the numerator of \(q_\star\) does not exceed \(W_\star\).  Thus the normalized weights are positive rationals summing to one and \(q_\star\in[0,1]\).  Since \(e=O(v^2)\), all numbers and the explicitly listed assignment matrix have polynomial binary length.

For a completion, write
\[
F=W_\star p(a,b).
\]
The actual row always contributes \(1\).  A guard row for vertex \(i\) replaces that vertex by a control, so it is in the upper tail exactly when
\[
r_i(b)\le r_C(b),
\]
where \(r_C\) is the common control rank.  Monotonicity of ordinary ranks in their underlying outcomes makes this equivalent to \(b_i\le0\).  If at least one guard fails, even granting every other row,
\[
F\le1+(v-1)A_\star+vB+e
<1+vA_\star,
\]
because \(A_\star=vB+e+1\).  This is strictly below the numerator of \(q_\star\).  Hence every successful completion passes all guards and has every vertex outcome at most zero.

Assume henceforth that all guards pass, and let \(t\) be the number of vertex outcomes equal to zero.  The other \(v-t\) vertex labels lie below the block consisting of the four controls and these \(t\) vertices.  The control midrank is therefore
\[
c=1+(v-t)+\frac{4+t-1}{2}=v+\frac52-\frac t2.
\]
All \(v+4\) vertex and control labels lie below the \(h\) anchors, whose common rank is
\[
r_H=1+(v+4)+\frac{h-1}{2}=v+4+\frac{h+1}{2}.
\]
A vertex row for \(i\) replaces \(i\) and one anchor by two controls.  It is in the tail precisely when
\[
r_i+r_H\le2c
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
r_i\le\frac{s+1}{2}-t,
\]
where the last equality uses \(h=2v-s\).  Similarly, an edge row for \(ij\) is in the tail precisely when
\[
r_i+r_j+2r_H\le4c
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
r_i+r_j\le s+1-2t.
\]

Let \(U\) be the set of vertices whose vertex rows pass, and put \(u=|U|\).  If \(u>0\), the midrank-bottom-block lemma and the preceding coordinatewise bound give
\[
\frac{u(u+1)}2
\le\sum_{i\in U}r_i
\le u\left(\frac{s+1}{2}-t\right),
\]
and hence \(u\le s-2t\le s\).  The conclusion \(u\le s\) is also immediate when \(u=0\).  If \(u\le s-1\), then, even if every edge row passes,
\[
F\le1+vA_\star+(s-1)B+e
<1+vA_\star+sB,
\]
because \(B=e+1\).  Such a completion cannot reach \(q_\star\).  Thus success forces \(u=s\), and \(u\le s-2t\) forces \(t=0\).

Each of the \(s\) labels in \(U\) now has rank at most \((s+1)/2\).  The final clause of the midrank-bottom-block lemma shows that \(U\) is exactly the unique lowest tied block and that all its ranks equal \((s+1)/2\).  Every vertex outside \(U\) consequently has rank at least \(s+1\).  With \(t=0\), the edge-row condition is \(r_i+r_j\le s+1\).  It holds when both endpoints are in \(U\), since their ranks sum to \(s+1\), and fails if an endpoint is outside \(U\), since the other rank is at least one.  Consequently
\[
F=1+vA_\star+sB+|E(U)|.
\]
Reaching \(q_\star\) is therefore equivalent to
\[
|E(U)|\ge\binom{s}{2}.
\]
As \(G\) is simple and \(|U|=s\), this holds exactly when \(U\) is an \(s\)-clique.

Conversely, if \(S\) is an \(s\)-clique, assign outcome \(-2\) to its vertex labels and \(-1\) to all remaining vertex labels.  Then all guards pass; \(S\) is the lowest tied block with rank \((s+1)/2\); exactly its \(s\) vertex rows pass; and exactly its \(\binom{s}{2}\) edge rows pass.  Thus \(F=1+vA_\star+sB+\binom{s}{2}\), attaining \(q_\star\).

The mapping is polynomial and preserves yes and no instances, so it proves NP-hardness.  Together with membership in \(\mathrm{NP}\), it proves NP-completeness with \(k=v\) missing realized-treated outcomes, four realized controls, two observed outcome values, \(n=3v-s+4\), and \(1+2v+|E|\) explicitly listed rows.  The proof uses the supplied rational weights essentially and makes no hardness claim for a uniform balance-generated support.
